identityReview: João Manuel Gonçalves Lourenço, born 5 March 1954 in Lobito, Angola; distinct from unrelated people with the same abbreviated name. Government and embassy biographies support birth and earlier provincial, parliamentary and defence service. The first national presidency began 26 September 2017, party leadership on 8 September 2018 and second presidential term on 15 September 2022. Current national presidency and party leadership are supported by November 2026 activity reports. The AU rotating chairmanship ended 14 February 2026; DRC–Rwanda mediation transferred to Gnassingbé in April 2025. Party leadership, national presidency, AU Assembly chair and AU Commission chair must remain separate.
lifeStatusEvidence: DW/Lusa’s 14 November 2026 report quotes Lourenço discussing succession at an actual industrial-technology-centre inauguration in Luanda, as Angola’s president and MPLA leader. The date is publication, not an independently verified interview date. The MPLA’s account of the 5 November meetings gives additional contemporaneous participation evidence. Neither depends only on a future invitation or an undated biography; no event video or portrait pixels were viewed.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read government and embassy biographical passages; Xinhua 2017 inauguration report; RTP/Lusa and Reuters/Euronews 2018 leadership reports; the Angola section of UN report S/2022/896; ENA February 2025 inauguration report; AU April 2025 Bureau and February 2026 succession releases; Togo April 2025 visit report; selected HRW World Report 2026 sections; DW/Lusa and MPLA November 2026 reports; selected historical constitutional articles; Commons descriptive/licensing/history text. No source photograph pixels were inspected.
corrections: Read the government biography birth paragraph and ministerial/provincial section: 5 March 1954, Lobito, Benguela; Moxico commissioner in 1983; Benguela 1986–1989; defence minister from 2014 until the 2017 campaign. Its header labels an election date of 24 August 2017, conflicting with contemporaneous Xinhua reporting of the 23 August general election. Do not adopt that header as either the polling or inauguration date. No birth certificate or complete presidential personnel decrees were inspected.

Read the foreign-ministry biography published by the Angolan embassy in Japan on 24 August 2020. It states Soviet military training in 1978–1982, heavy-artillery specialisation and a master’s degree in historical sciences there, without identifying the specific award institution/date. It gives first vice-president of the National Assembly in 2003–2014, defence appointment in 2014 and earlier provincial posts. The 2020 publication date is not a new appointment. Do not turn a master’s into a doctorate, guess the university, or rely on its dated present-tense roles to establish 2026 incumbency.

Read the contemporaneous Xinhua 26 September 2017 report. It confirms the completed inauguration, succession to José Eduardo dos Santos and the 23 August general election. The predecessor’s long presidential tenure is separate from his continuing party leadership. The article’s remarks about unanimous national support are attributed ceremonial rhetoric and are not treated as public-opinion findings. No event video or photograph pixels were inspected.

Read RTP’s Lusa account of the MPLA leadership election, its party congress procedure, presidency since 26 September 2017, and the new party leader’s anti-corruption commitments. Promises to combat nepotism and impunity are not proof of eradication. It reports 98.58 percent, while Reuters reports 98.59 percent; the public dossier omits that minor conflicting percentage rather than silently choosing one. Party-election commission claims of a fair internal vote are not independent election certification.

Read Reuters’s report carried by Euronews, dated 8 September 2018. It distinguishes the 2017 national presidency from the 2018 party succession and records an unopposed internal leadership election. Discussion of prospective cabinet changes and economic diversification is not evidence that all reforms succeeded. Historic accusations or suspect status concerning dos Santos family members are not imported as current criminal verdicts, and the old currency/IMF figures are not used as 2026 economic indicators.

Read the Angola subsection and relevant context in UN Secretary-General report S/2022/896 dated 1 December 2022, paragraphs 2–3. It gives polling on 24 August, announced MPLA vote share of 51.17 percent on 29 August, opposition complaints, the Constitutional Court’s 8 September finality ruling, and the 15 September presidential/vice-presidential inauguration. It also records observer concerns about electoral administration and media coverage. Do not conflate a court’s confirmation of results with absence of electoral criticism, polling with inauguration, or party vote share with a separate personal presidential ballot. The whole regional report and original election judgments were not audited.

Read ENA’s short contemporaneous 15 February 2025 report, explicitly stating the AU chairmanship was assumed that day at the opening of the 38th summit. It supersedes a later March publication/profile date as evidence for the beginning of this one-year rotating office. This office is separate from the African Union Commission chairperson and from an AU peace-champion designation.

Read the AU’s 5 April 2025 Assembly Bureau meeting record. Lourenço chaired the virtual meeting, explained his intended withdrawal from DRC–Rwanda mediation, proposed Faure Gnassingbé and obtained Bureau endorsement. The record expressly describes formal Assembly concurrence as still required; 5 April endorsement alone is not the final appointment. Do not carry the mediation office forward indefinitely or claim the conflict ended. The Commission chair attending the meeting is a different official and institutional office.

Read the Togolese presidency’s 16 April 2025 report of Gnassingbé’s actual Luanda visit and talks with Lourenço as newly appointed AU mediator. It dates formal designation to 12 April, distinct from the 5 April proposal and subsequent news publication dates. The public chronology uses April without unnecessary day-level precision for the handover. The official account’s praise of diplomatic achievements and hopes for an effective ceasefire are not independent proof that peace was achieved or all armed groups complied.

Read the African Union’s 14 February 2026 summit release confirming that Évariste Ndayishimiye succeeded Lourenço in the rotating chairmanship. The AU’s current roster separately lists Burundi for February 2026–February 2027 and Angola for February 2025–February 2026. The public role no longer calls Lourenço current AU chair. Neither the Assembly chair nor Angola’s rapporteur position is equivalent to chair of the AU Commission.

Read the heading and selected assembly, press-freedom and fair-trial sections of Human Rights Watch’s World Report 2026 Angola chapter. The page explicitly covers events of 2025. Its accounts of protest policing, arbitrary arrests and media restrictions are attributed to the organisation, not described as 2026 events or judicial findings of Lourenço’s personal guilt. It also reports the police announcement of an investigation and their denial of shoot-to-kill orders. No current outcome of each investigation or individual criminal case was verified; disputed casualty totals and Cabinda allegations are not imported into the public profile.

Read DW Africa/Lusa’s report published on 14 November 2026, including quoted remarks made at an industrial-technology-centre inauguration in Luanda. It identifies him as current president and MPLA leader and distinguishes his sole admitted party-leadership candidacy from the as-yet-unannounced candidate for the 2027 national election. The date in the timeline is the report publication date; the exact event/interview date was not independently established. The report discusses a planned December congress, not a completed re-election. Its two-term-limit context is consistent with the constitutional text, without projecting unverified future rule changes or naming a successor.

Read the MPLA’s official report: webpage publication 7 November 2026, dateline 6 November, and Central Committee meeting/approval on Thursday 5 November. It records approval of Lourenço’s candidacy for party president and his chairing of the preceding Political Bureau meeting. Approval is not a completed leadership election and is not nomination for the 2027 national presidency. The party’s praise of its leadership is not independent validation of democratic or economic outcomes.

Read the Constitute Project’s English rendering of the 2010 Constitution, selected Articles 106, 108–114. Article 109 ties presidential election to the first name on the national list of the party or coalition with most votes, while Article 106 describes universal direct suffrage. Therefore the accurate distinction is absence of a separate presidential ballot, not a claim that voters are entirely excluded or that parliament directly elects the president. Article 113 states a five-year term and a two-term limit. This is a historical constitutional edition, not a full audit of all subsequent amendments; contemporary DW reporting supplies current electoral context.

additionalConsulted.access: Read current chair description and roster, confirming a one-year head-of-state/government office and Ndayishimiye as current chair in 2026.

Read dated outgoing-chair handover speech landing page. Linked speech PDFs and video were not opened; title and date corroborate the completed succession but do not establish every claim in the speech.
Read indexed 24 March 2025 report of announced withdrawal from mediation. Full article not opened; distinguish announcement from subsequent April formal appointment and actual visit.
Search-indexed profile date begins 11 March 2025. Do not treat a page/profile date as assumption of AU office; the contemporaneous ENA report specifies 15 February.

Indexed AU 26 September 2017 inauguration account, but direct opening returned an 403 failure. An attempted English release path also failed. Do not claim full-body reading; readable Xinhua and later RTP reporting support the date.
Search-indexed corroboration of February 2025 handover; opening returned 403. ENA supplied the readable contemporaneous report.
Read description, dimensions, creator and licence requirements, and 16 July 2018 upload history, without image pixels.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified human/native-language review. No birth or degree certificates, complete original electoral court files, complete subsequent constitutional-amendment audit, independent corruption/economic outcome audit, current investigation outcomes or portrait pixels were inspected. Source percentages conflict slightly for the 2018 internal party vote and are omitted. Distinguish announcement, nomination, election, inauguration and handover; report human-rights claims with attribution and correct coverage year. Refresh current offices and events before publication.

portraitReview.unresolved: Read Commons description, creator attribution, reuse instructions, licence and upload history. Caption and metadata identify a 4 July 2018 European Parliament visit in Strasbourg; 16 July 2018 is upload time. Original dimensions are 2121×2557, 2.08 MB; the absent legacy 201261-byte cache record is not evidence of possessing this original. Preserve creator/homepage and licence links, indicate changes and meet share-alike terms for adaptations; do not relabel the German 3.0 licence as public domain or CC BY 4.0. One original download attempt on 18 November returned curl exit 22, 403 and reported HTTP 000. No image pixels were inspected, so identity, original colour, cropping and sharpness remain unverified.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages reviewed against Chinese and English. Preserve 1954 birthday and Lobito; Soviet training dates versus unspecified degree-award date; provincial posts, first parliamentary vice-presidency and defence ministry; 2017 presidency versus 2018 party leadership; most-voted national list without a separate presidential ballot; 2022 polling, court confirmation and inauguration; 2025–2026 rotating AU chair versus Commission chair; April mediation succession versus resolved conflict; November party candidacy approval versus a completed election or national nomination; report publication date versus exact interview date; 2026 HRW report covering events of 2025; political promises and NGO criticisms versus proven outcomes or personal criminal judgments.
